title: How the FlexLine Late Fee Is Figured from the Unpaid Part
content:
**Desk ruling — FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit.** The way the late fee is figured follows the unpaid part of the minimum payment and the days from the due date to the booking date:

- below 100.00 USD on a line fewer than 30 days late, the figured fee is 25% of the unpaid part, rounded to the cent, but never more than the tier's late fee (the smaller of the two);
- 250.00 USD or more, the figured fee is the larger of the tier's late fee and 5% of the unpaid part, rounded to the cent;
- any other unpaid part below 250.00 USD (100.00 USD or more, or below 100.00 USD on a line 30 days late or more) is figured at the tier's late fee as a flat amount.

The unpaid part is the line's amount past due on the booking date; the days late are the calendar days from the due date charged to the booking date. Each rounding to the cent takes an exact half cent to the even cent.

## Decision table

| Unpaid part | Days late | Figured fee |
|---|---|---|
| below 100.00 | fewer than 30 | smaller of 25% of the unpaid part and the tier's late fee |
| below 100.00 | 30 or more | tier's late fee |
| 100.00 to 249.99 | any | tier's late fee |
| 250.00 or more | any | larger of the tier's late fee and 5% of the unpaid part |

## Hypothetical cases (tier late fee of 25.00 USD)

- Unpaid 72.00, 12 days late: 25% is 18.00, below 25.00, so 18.00.
- Unpaid 72.00, 30 days late: 25.00.
- Unpaid 180.00: 25.00.
- Unpaid 250.00: 5% is 12.50, so the larger is 25.00.
- Unpaid 640.00: 5% is 32.00, above 25.00, so 32.00.
